transcript: Hey guys, what's going on? It's Dave. Welcome back. I want to thank everybodywho's shown the love and support for the channel. Appreciate it, guys. If youshare the video, it helps out a lot. Thanks. Well, thePacific Link Pipeline, the newly proposed one that Carney was talkingabout, well, guess what? The Indigenous don't like it. What a freaking surprise,right? They're saying that it's going to cross the land and it's going to affectwater and hunting and this and that. And you know, there's the duty to consult.Well, hold on a second. First thing, the duty to consult, that's just what itsounds like. You consult. You ask. That's it. You don't have to take anyrecommendations from the Indigenous at all. All it is is a duty to ask. Nextthing, the Indigenous people are going to get minimum minimum 10% ownershipbecause the federal government is going to offer Indigenous communities aminimum of 10% equity stake in the project.And anything any loan guarantees that they need, they're going to get it. Butthere's something else that everybody's kind of forgetting. Anymajor um project that the government has thefederal government has, 5% of the total price of that project goes right to theIndigenous. So, what are they bellyaching about?Like, come on. I think I think, my own opinion,that they're just after more money. Make a stink or don't have the pipelinewhatsoever. I think they want the pipeline. I just think they want moremoney. Just my opinion.Let me know what you think. You guys take care. Please be safe.
